questions.question: The HCF of 45, 78 and 117 is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Check the **difference** between the closest numbers: 117 − 78 = 39.

The **HCF** must be a factor of 39 (Factors: 1, 3, 13, 39).

Test the highest factor: 39 does not divide 45. 13 does not divide 45.

3 divides 45, 78, and 117 perfectly.

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers are 45, 78, and 117.

**Formula Used:** **Prime Factorization Method** for finding **Highest Common Factor (HCF)**.

⇒ Prime factors of 45 = 3 × 3 × 5 = 3² × 5

⇒ Prime factors of 78 = 2 × 3 × 13

⇒ Prime factors of 117 = 3 × 3 × 13 = 3² × 13

⇒ Common prime factor in all three numbers = 3

⇒ HCF = Lowest power of common prime factor = 3¹

⇒ HCF = 3

**∴ The correct answer is 3.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Definition of HCF

The **Highest Common Factor (HCF)** is the largest positive integer that divides each of the integers without leaving a remainder.

Relationship between HCF and LCM

For two numbers a and b, **HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b) = a × b**. This property does not directly apply to three or more numbers.

Division Method for HCF

Divide the larger number by the smaller one, then divide the previous divisor by the remainder until the remainder is zero. The last divisor is the HCF.</p

questions.question:
Which of the options represents the correct and balanced chemical equation for the reaction between a metallic oxide and an acid? 

CuO + HCl → ______ + ________
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CuO + 2HCI → CuCl2 + H2O**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When a metallic oxide reacts with an acid, it typically forms a salt and water.
 
• Copper (II) oxide (CuO) is a black solid that reacts with hydrochloric acid (HCl) to form copper (II) chloride (CuCl2), a greenish-blue solution, and water (H2O).
 
• The balanced chemical equation for this reaction is CuO + 2HCl → CuCl2 + H2O.
 
• Balancing the equation ensures that the number of atoms of each element is the same on both sides of the equation, adhering to the law of conservation of mass.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Metallic Oxides:**

 
 
• Metallic oxides are compounds consisting of a metal and oxygen.
 
• They are typically basic and react with acids to form salts and water.
 
 
 
• **Hydrochloric Acid (HCl):**
 
 
• Hydrochloric acid is a strong acid, commonly used in various chemical reactions.
 
• It is highly corrosive and should be handled with care.
 
 
 
• **Balancing Chemical Equations:**
 
 
• Balancing chemical equations is essential for representing the law of conservation of mass.
 
• It ensures that the number of atoms for each element is equal on both the reactant and product sides.
 
 
 
• **Copper (II) Chloride (CuCl2):**
 
 
• Copper (II) chloride is an inorganic compound with the formula CuCl2.
 
• It appears as a greenish-blue solid and is used in various industrial and chemical applications.

questions.question: The list price of an article is Rs. 1200 and a discount of 15% is offered on the list price. The selling price of the article is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Discount%** = 15% ⇒ **Selling Price** = 85% of **List Price**.

SP = 1200 × (100 − 15) ÷ 100.

SP = 1200 × 85 ÷ 100 = 12 × 85.

SP = 1020.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1020.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **List Price (MP)** = Rs. 1200, **Discount Rate** = 15%.

**Formulas:** **Discount** = MP × Discount% | **SP** = MP − Discount.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/638758d9c08b2257c2c5f26020304f7002e8ad26c944f813ef4db9b1a816a51c.png] 

⇒ **Discount Amount** = 15% of 1200 = (15 ÷ 100) × 1200 = 180.

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = 1200 − 180 = 1020.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1020.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price and List Price

The **List Price** is the price at which the article is listed for sale before any discount. It is functionally the same as the **Marked Price (MP)**.

Calculating SP with multiple discounts

If two successive discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, SP = MP × (100 − d₁)/100 × (100 − d₂)/100.</p

questions.question: When a body of mass m is raised to a height H against gravity, the potential energy of the body is:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**increased by an amount mgH**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Potential energy (PE) is the energy possessed by an object due to its position relative to a reference point, often the Earth.
 
• When a body of mass m is raised to a height H against gravity, the work done against the gravitational force is stored as potential energy.
 
• The formula for gravitational potential energy is PE = m * g * H, where g is the acceleration due to gravity (approximately 9.8 m/s² on Earth).
 
• Thus, raising a body of mass m to a height H increases its potential energy by an amount equal to m * g * H.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gravitational Force**

 
 
• It is a force that attracts any two objects with mass towards each other.
 
• The gravitational force between two objects is proportional to the product of their masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
 
 
 
• **Potential Energy**
 
 
• This is the energy possessed by a body due to its position or state.
 
• It is a form of mechanical energy, alongside kinetic energy.
 
 
 
• **Work-Energy Principle**
 
 
• This principle states that the work done on an object is equal to the change in its kinetic energy.
 
• In the context of potential energy, work done against gravity is stored as potential energy.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Energy**
 
 
• This fundamental principle states that energy cannot be created or destroyed, only transformed from one form to another.
 
• In an ideal system, the total energy remains constant over time.

questions.question:
Why does the following action take place in plants?

Plant cells change shape by changing the amount of water in them, resulting in swelling or shrinking, and therefore in changing shape.

options.text: In immediate response to some stimulus

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**In immediate response to some stimulus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Plant cells change shape in response to external stimuli such as light, gravity, touch, and water availability.
 
• This process, known as turgor movement, involves the uptake or release of water in the cell's vacuoles, causing the cell to swell or shrink.
 
• Examples of such movements include the opening and closing of stomata, and the rapid movements of mimosa leaves when touched.
 
• These responses help plants adapt to their environment and optimize conditions for processes like photosynthesis and water conservation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Turgor Pressure**

 
 
• The pressure exerted by the fluid (water) inside the cell against the cell wall.
 
• It is crucial for maintaining the structural integrity and rigidity of plant cells.
 
 
 
• **Stomata**
 
 
• Small openings on the surfaces of leaves and stems that allow gas exchange.
 
• Stomata open and close in response to environmental conditions to regulate water loss and gas exchange.
 
 
 
• **Phototropism**
 
 
• The growth of plant organs in response to light direction.
 
• Plants bend towards the light source to maximize photosynthesis.
 
 
 
• **Hydrotropism**
 
 
• The growth response of plant roots towards moisture.
 
• It enables roots to seek out water sources to sustain the plant.
 
 
 
• **Thigmotropism**
 
 
• The directional growth movement of plants in response to touch or physical contact.
 
• Common in climbing plants, allowing them to wrap around structures for support.

questions.question: What least natural number must be added to 6072 to make it a perfect square?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Estimate the **square root** of 6072: 70² = 4900 and 80² = 6400.

Since 6072 is close to 6400, test **78²** = (80 − 2)² = 6400 − 320 + 4 = 6084.

The next **perfect square** after 6072 is 6084.

Least number to be added = 6084 − 6072 = 12.

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Number = 6072

**Formula:** Required Number = (Next Perfect Square) − (Given Number)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/964a587bc69f3e37b6ca11bc748d42163f22beac51a541b79928c6ea15fa8d26.png] 

**Step-by-step Calculation:**

⇒ Approximate square root: √6072 ≈ 77.92

⇒ The integer immediately greater than 77.92 is 78.

⇒ Calculate 78² = 78 × 78

⇒ 78² = 6084

⇒ Difference = 6084 − 6072

⇒ Difference = 12

**∴ The correct answer is 12.**

**__Additional Information__**

Perfect Square Unit Digits

A perfect square always ends in 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, or 9. It never ends in 2, 3, 7, or 8.

Long Division Method

To find what to add, perform long division; the square of (quotient + 1) minus the original number gives the required value.

Digital Root Property

The digital root (sum of digits reduced to a single digit) of a perfect square is always 1, 4, 7, or 9.</p

questions.question: Which of the following organisms reproduce by spore formation?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

• **Rhizopus** is a genus of common saprophytic fungi on plants and specialized parasites on animals.
 
• It reproduces asexually through the formation of spores, which are produced in sporangia.
 
• The spores are released into the air and can germinate when they land on a suitable substrate, leading to the formation of new mycelium.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Spores**

 
 
• Spores are reproductive units that can develop into a new organism without fusion with another reproductive unit.
 
• They are typically single-celled and can be produced sexually or asexually.
 
• Spores are highly resistant to environmental stresses such as heat, UV radiation, and desiccation.
 
 
 
• **Spore Formation in Fungi**
 
 
• Fungi reproduce by forming spores, which can be dispersed by wind, water, or animals.
 
• Spore formation allows fungi to spread and colonize new environments efficiently.
 
• Fungi can produce a vast number of spores, increasing the likelihood of successful reproduction.
 
 
 
• **Types of Spore Formation**
 
 
• There are different types of spores, including sporangiospores, conidiospores, and zygospores.
 
• Sporangiospores are formed inside sporangia, while conidiospores are formed at the tips of specialized hyphae called conidiophores.
 
• Zygospores are thick-walled resting spores formed by the fusion of two similar gametangia.
 
 
 
• **Rhizopus in Biotechnology**
 
 
• Rhizopus species are used in the production of various industrial products, such as organic acids and enzymes.
 
• They play a role in the fermentation process for certain traditional foods, such as tempeh and sufu.
 
• Their ability to produce large quantities of spores makes them valuable in biotechnological applications.

questions.solution:

• Heating ethanol at 443 K with excess concentrated sulfuric acid results in the dehydration of ethanol.
 
• The dehydration process involves the removal of a water molecule from ethanol.
 
• This reaction produces ethene (C₂H₄), a colorless and flammable gas.
 
• The chemical equation for this reaction is: C₂H₅OH → C₂H₄ + H₂O.
 
• Concentrated sulfuric acid acts as a catalyst in this reaction.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• A chemical reaction in which water is removed from a compound.
 
• Commonly occurs in the presence of a strong acid like sulfuric acid.
 
• Used to convert alcohols to alkenes.
 
 
 
• **Sulfuric Acid (H₂SO₄)**
 
 
• A strong mineral acid with strong dehydrating properties.
 
• Commonly used in the chemical industry as a catalyst.
 
• Can cause severe burns; hence, handle with care.
 
 
 
• **Ethene (C₂H₄)**
 
 
• Also known as ethylene.
 
• Used as a precursor in the production of polyethylene, a common plastic.
 
• Acts as a plant hormone involved in the ripening of fruits.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Ethene**
 
 
• Widely used in the manufacture of plastics and synthetic rubber.
 
• Employed in the production of ethanol and other chemicals.
 
• Utilized in agriculture to promote the ripening of fruits.

For a **3-digit number** abc to be divisible by 11, the sum of extreme digits minus middle digit should be 0 or 11.

questions.question: The LCM of the numbers 5, 12.5 and 0.05 is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

To find the **LCM of decimals**, make the number of decimal places equal: 5.00, 12.50, and 0.05.

Remove the decimal and treat them as integers: **500, 1250, and 5**.

LCM(5, 500, 1250) ⇒ 1250 is not divisible by 500, but 1250 × 2 = 2500 is divisible by 500 and 5.

Place the decimal back (2 places): 2500 → 25.00.

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Numbers are 5, 12.5 and 0.05.

**Formula Used:** LCM of Fractions = (LCM of Numerators) ÷ (HCF of Denominators)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/66a70e8ae8d6cd529820a695853b883639cbef6086a87e7f04480c95cfbf9f0a.png] 

⇒ Convert decimals to fractions: 5/1, 125/10, 5/100.

⇒ Simplify fractions: 5/1, 25/2, 1/20.

⇒ LCM of Numerators (5, 25, 1) = 25.

⇒ HCF of Denominators (1, 2, 20) = 1.

⇒ Required LCM = 25 ÷ 1 = 25.

**∴ The correct answer is 25.**

**__Additional Information__**

LCM of Fractions

The Least Common Multiple of fractions is calculated as (LCM of numerators) ÷ (HCF of denominators).

HCF of Fractions

The Highest Common Factor of fractions is calculated as (HCF of numerators) ÷ (LCM of denominators).

Decimal Conversion Rule

To find LCM/HCF of decimals, it is often safer to convert them into like decimals (same number of decimal places) before treating them as integers.</p

Rate = 12.5% = 1/8. **Principal** (P) = 8 units, **Interest** (I) for 1 year = 1 unit.

Interest for 2 years = 1 × 2 = 2 units. **Amount** (A) = P + I = 8 + 2 = 10 units.

Given 10 units = ₹8250 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹825.

Simple Interest for 1 year = 1 unit = ₹825.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 825.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Rate (R) = 12.5%, Time (T) = 2 years, Amount (A) = ₹8,250.

**Formula:** Amount = Principal + Simple Interest ⇒ A = P + (P × R × T)/100

⇒ 8250 = P + (P × 12.5 × 2)/100

⇒ 8250 = P + (P × 25)/100

⇒ 8250 = P + 0.25P ⇒ 1.25P = 8250

⇒ P = 8250 / 1.25 = ₹6,600

⇒ Total SI for 2 years = 8250 − 6600 = ₹1,650

⇒ SI for 1 year = 1650 ÷ 2 = ₹825

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 825.**

Simple Interest Concept

Simple interest is calculated only on the **Principal** amount, meaning the interest remains constant every year if the rate and principal are unchanged.

Amount Formula

The total **Amount** after T years is A = P(1 + RT/100), where P is principal, R is rate per annum, and T is time in years.

Converting percentage rates to fractions (e.g., 12.5% = 1/8) simplifies calculations by treating the denominator as the **Principal** and numerator as **Interest** per unit time.

questions.question: (x+(1)/(x)) (x-(1)/(x)) (x²+(1)/(x²)) (x⁴+(1)/(x⁴)) is equal to:

__Shortcut Trick__

Apply the algebraic identity **(a + b)(a − b) = a² − b²** successively.

(x + 1/x)(x − 1/x) = x² − 1/x²

(x² − 1/x²)(x² + 1/x²) = x⁴ − 1/x⁴

(x⁴ − 1/x⁴)(x⁴ + 1/x⁴) = x⁸ − 1/x⁸

**∴ The correct answer is x⁸ − 1/x⁸.**

**Given:** (x + 1/x)(x − 1/x)(x² + 1/x²)(x⁴ + 1/x⁴)

⇒ Step 3: Multiply result with (x⁴ + 1/x⁴) = (x⁴)² − (1/x⁴)² = x⁸ − 1/x⁸

**∴ The correct answer is x⁸ − 1/x⁸.**

**__Additional Information__**

Algebraic Identities

Standard identity: (a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b² and (a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b².

Power Rule

When multiplying terms with the same base, add exponents: xa × xb = xa⁺b. For powers: (xa)b = xa×b.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**(i), (ii) and (iii)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• (i) The term "translocation" is indeed used for the transport of soluble products of photosynthesis, not insoluble products.
 
• (ii) Respiration is the metabolic process of breaking down glucose to release energy, not the evaporative loss of water through stomata. The process of water loss through stomata is known as transpiration.
 
• (iii) Photosynthesis requires sunlight to convert substances into stored forms of energy (glucose). The given statement incorrectly states that it occurs in the absence of sunlight.
 
• All three statements (i), (ii), and (iii) are factually incorrect based on fundamental biological concepts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Translocation in Plants**

 
 
• Translocation refers to the movement of soluble products of photosynthesis, such as sugars, from the leaves to other parts of the plant.
 
• This process occurs through the phloem tissue.
 
 
 
• **Respiration in Plants**

questions.question: The average monthly income of P and Q is Rs. 5,050. The average monthly income of Q and R is Rs. 6,250 and the average monthly income of P and R is Rs. 5,200. The monthly income of P (in Rs.) is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Sum of (P+Q), (Q+R), and (P+R) = 2 × (P+Q+R).

P + Q = 5050 × 2 = 10100

Q + R = 6250 × 2 = 12500

P + R = 5200 × 2 = 10400

P = [(P+Q) + (P+R) − (Q+R)] ÷ 2 = [10100 + 10400 − 12500] ÷ 2 = 8000 ÷ 2 = 4000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Average of **P and Q** = ₹5,050; Average of **Q and R** = ₹6,250; Average of **P and R** = ₹5,200.

**Formula Used:** Total Sum = Average × Number of entities.

⇒ P + Q = 5050 × 2 = 10100 --- (i)

⇒ Q + R = 6250 × 2 = 12500 --- (ii)

⇒ P + R = 5200 × 2 = 10400 --- (iii)

⇒ Adding (i), (ii), and (iii): 2(P + Q + R) = 10100 + 12500 + 10400 = 33000

⇒ P + Q + R = 33000 ÷ 2 = 16500

⇒ Monthly income of P = (P + Q + R) − (Q + R) = 16500 − 12500

⇒ P = 4000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹4000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Income Formula

Average = (Sum of all observations) ÷ (Total number of observations). In this case, Sum = Average × 2.

Cyclic Sums

For equations of type A+B, B+C, and C+A, the value of A = [(A+B) + (C+A) − (B+C)] ÷ 2.

Combined Average

The average of all three (P, Q, R) is the sum of the three pair-averages divided by 3, which is 16500 ÷ 3 = ₹5,500.

• These oxides exhibit neutrality due to the lack of acidic or basic properties.

questions.question: A body, starting from rest, falls from a building and reaches the ground in 2 secs. What will be the velocity of the body when it reaches the ground? (Acceleration due to gravity = 10 ms⁻² )

• The acceleration due to gravity (g) is 10 m/s².

• Substituting the values, v = 0 + (10 m/s² * 2 s) = 20 m/s.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Free Fall:**
 
 
• It is the motion of a body where gravity is the only force acting upon it.
 
• In a vacuum, all objects fall at the same rate regardless of their masses.
 
 
 
• **Equations of Motion:**
 
 
• These equations describe the relationship between displacement, velocity, acceleration, and time.
 
• Commonly used equations include: v = u + at, s = ut + 0.5at², and v² = u² + 2as.

• It is the constant speed that a freely falling object eventually reaches when the resistance of the medium prevents further acceleration.
 
• For objects falling through air, terminal velocity depends on the object's size, shape, and mass.

questions.question: Simplify (2.46times 2.46-1.46times 1.46)/(2.46-1.46) and select the most appropriate fraction.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The expression is in the form of **(a² − b²) / (a − b)**.

Algebraic identity: **a² − b² = (a − b)(a + b)**.

Therefore, **(a − b)(a + b) / (a − b) = a + b**.

Result = **2.46 + 1.46 = 3.92**.

Converting to fraction: **3.92 = 392/100**.

**∴ The correct answer is 392/100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Expression = ((2.46 × 2.46) − (1.46 × 1.46)) ÷ (2.46 − 1.46)

**Formula Used:** a² − b² = (a + b)(a − b)

⇒ Let **a = 2.46** and **b = 1.46**.

⇒ Expression = (a² − b²) / (a − b)

⇒ Expression = ((a + b)(a − b)) / (a − b)

⇒ Expression = a + b

⇒ Expression = 2.46 + 1.46

⇒ Expression = 3.92

⇒ 3.92 = 392 / 100

**∴ The correct answer is 392/100.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**Algebraic Identities**

Square of sum: **(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²**. Square of difference: **(a − b)² = a² − 2ab + b²**.

**Decimal to Fraction**

To convert a **decimal** to a **fraction**, place the number over a power of 10 based on the number of decimal places (e.g., 0.xy = xy/100).</p

questions.question: If the ratio of the volume of two spheres is 1 : 8, then the ratio of their surface area is:

Ratio of **Volumes** (V₁ : V₂) = 1 : 8

Ratio of **Radii** (r₁ : r₂) = ³√1 : ³√8 = 1 : 2

Ratio of **Surface Areas** (A₁ : A₂) = (r₁)² : (r₂)² = 1² : 2² = 1 : 4

**∴ The correct answer is 1 : 4.**

⇒ Ratio of Surface Areas = (4πr₁²) / (4πr₂²)

Dimensional Proportionality

For any similar 3D shapes, if the ratio of **linear dimensions** (radius, side) is a:b, then the ratio of **surface areas** is a²:b² and the ratio of **volumes** is a³:b³.

• **Balancing Chemical Equations:**
 
 
• The process of balancing chemical equations involves making sure that the number of atoms for each element is the same on both sides of the equation.

• **Oxidation-Reduction (Redox) Reactions:**

Time taken initially (T₁) = 60 minutes

Target number of litchis (L₂) = 35

**Formula Used:**

Since the pace is constant, the ratio of litchis eaten to time taken remains constant:

L₁ ÷ T₁ = L₂ ÷ T₂

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4bce527e600261bd35a98386ea5a8facbd348c359feeb88572f98b25c5fb3377.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ 21 ÷ 60 = 35 ÷ T₂

⇒ T₂ = (35 × 60) ÷ 21

⇒ T₂ = (5 × 60) ÷ 3

⇒ T₂ = 5 × 20

⇒ T₂ = 100 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 100 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct Proportion

When two quantities are in direct proportion, an increase in one leads to a proportional increase in the other. The ratio x ÷ y remains constant throughout.

Unitary Method

A problem-solving method where we first find the value of a single unit (by dividing), and then multiply this individual value to find the required total value.</p

questions.question: If 9 : 12 :: 12 : k, then find the value of k + 1.

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

For a **continued proportion** a : b :: b : c, the formula is b² = a × c.

Here, 12² = 9 × k ⇒ 144 = 9 × k ⇒ k = 16.

Value of k + 1 = 16 + 1 = 17.

**∴ The correct answer is 17.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 9 : 12 :: 12 : k

**Formula:** Product of Extremes = Product of Means

⇒ 9 × k = 12 × 12

⇒ 9k = 144

⇒ k = 144 ÷ 9

⇒ k = 16

**To find:** Value of k + 1

⇒ 16 + 1 = 17

Mean Proportional

Third Proportional

In the proportion a : b :: b : c, the term **c** is called the **third proportional** and c = b²/a.

Fourth Proportional

In a : b :: c : d, the term **d** is the **fourth proportional** where d = (b × c)/a.</p

questions.question: Triveni’s salary was first decreased by 16% and subsequently increased by 25%. The net percentage change in her salary was:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Apply the **Successive Percentage Formula**: Net Change % = a + b + (ab/100)

Here, a = −16% (decrease) and b = +25% (increase).

Net Change = −16 + 25 + [(−16 × 25) / 100]

Net Change = 9 − (400 / 100) = 9 − 4 = +5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5% increase.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial decrease = 16%, Subsequent increase = 25%

**Formula Used:** Final Value = Initial Value × (100 ± x)/100 × (100 ± y)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/564cfb228acd9c62c288ffb86bc22f2c273473d86f2a18504e5f8d4ba0113b44.png] 

⇒ Let initial salary = 100

⇒ Salary after 16% decrease = 100 − 16 = 84

⇒ Salary after 25% increase = 84 + (25% of 84)

⇒ 25% of 84 = 84/4 = 21

⇒ Final salary = 84 + 21 = 105

⇒ Net change = 105 − 100 = 5

⇒ Percentage change = (5 / 100) × 100 = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5% increase.**

**__Additional Information__**

Successive Percentage Change

When a value is changed by x% and then by y% successively, the effective change is [x + y + (xy/100)]%.

Fraction Method

Convert percentages to fractions: 16% decrease = 21/25 multiplier; 25% increase = 5/4 multiplier. Net effect = 21/25 × 5/4 = 21/20 = 105/100.

Successive Discounts

Used in Profit & Loss, net discount = d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂ / 100)%.</p

questions.question: An atom has 17 protons, 18 neutrons, and 17 electrons. What is its mass number?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**35**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The mass number of an atom is calculated by summing the number of protons and neutrons in its nucleus.
 
• In this case, the atom has 17 protons and 18 neutrons.
 
• The formula for the mass number (A) is A = Number of Protons + Number of Neutrons.
 
• Therefore, the mass number of this atom is 17 + 18 = 35.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Atomic Number**

 
 
• The atomic number is the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• It determines the chemical properties of an element and its place in the periodic table.
 
• For this atom, the atomic number is 17, indicating it is chlorine (Cl).
 
 
 
• **Isotopes**
 
 
• Isotopes are variants of a particular chemical element that have different numbers of neutrons.
 
• Chlorine has two stable isotopes: Cl-35 and Cl-37.
 
• Isotopes have the same atomic number but different mass numbers.
 
 
 
• **Neutrons**
 
 
• Neutrons are neutral particles found in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• They contribute to the mass of the atom but do not affect its chemical properties.
 
• The number of neutrons in this atom is 18.
 
 
 
• **Electrons**
 
 
• Electrons are negatively charged particles orbiting the nucleus of an atom.
 
• In a neutral atom, the number of electrons equals the number of protons.
 
• For this atom, there are 17 electrons.

questions.question: Which of the following is the best example of a heterogeneous mixture?

options.text: Mixture of iron chloride and iron fillings

The correct answer is __**Mixture of iron chloride and iron fillings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A heterogeneous mixture is one in which the components can be visibly distinguished and are not uniformly distributed.
 
• The mixture of iron chloride and iron fillings is an example of a heterogeneous mixture because the two substances remain distinct and separate.
 
• In this mixture, iron fillings can be seen as solid particles distinct from the iron chloride.
 
• Such mixtures do not have a uniform composition throughout and the different components can be easily separated by physical methods like filtration or magnetic separation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Homogeneous Mixture:**

 
 
• It is a mixture in which the composition is uniform throughout.
 
• Examples include solutions like salt in water or sugar in water where the solute is completely dissolved.
 
• Homogeneous mixtures cannot be separated by simple physical methods.
 
 
 
• **Methods of Separation:**
 
 
• **Filtration:** Used to separate an insoluble solid from a liquid.
 
• **Magnetic Separation:** Useful for separating magnetic materials from non-magnetic ones.
 
• **Evaporation:** Used to separate a dissolved solid from a liquid by evaporating the liquid.
 
 
 
• **Colloids:**
 
 
• A type of homogeneous mixture where the particle size is intermediate between a true solution and a suspension.
 
• Examples include milk, fog, and jelly.
 
 
 
• **Suspensions:**
 
 
• A type of heterogeneous mixture where the particles are large enough to settle out over time.
 
• Examples include sand in water or dust in air.

• It is crucial for the perception and interpretation of sounds.

questions.question: A and B can do a piece of work in 12 days and 16 days, respectively. Both work for 3 days and then A goes away. Find how long will B take to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let **Total Work** be LCM(12, 16) = 48 units.

Efficiency of **A** = 4 units/day and **B** = 3 units/day.

Work done in **3 days** = 3 × (4 + 3) = 21 units.

**Remaining work** = 48 − 21 = 27 units.

Time taken by **B** = 27 ÷ 3 = 9 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Time taken by **A** = 12 days, Time taken by **B** = 16 days. Work period = 3 days.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Efficiency × Time; Efficiency = 1 ÷ Time taken.

questions.question: A and B complete a work in 2 days. If A alone can do it in 4 days then, B alone can do 17-times of the same work in ______________(days).
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__
Time taken by **B alone** to complete 1 unit of work = (A × B) ÷ (A − (A & B))

⇒ Time for **B** = (4 × 2) ÷ (4 − 2) = 8 ÷ 2 = **4 days**.

For **17-times** of the same work, time taken = 4 × 17 = **68 days**.

**∴ The correct answer is 68 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **(A + B)** = 2 days

Time taken by **A** alone = 4 days

 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency**
 **A + B** 2 4 units 2
 **A** 4 1
**Calculations:**

⇒ **Efficiency of B** = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of A

⇒ **Efficiency of B** = 2 − 1 = **1 unit/day**

⇒ Time taken by **B** to do 1-time work = Total Work ÷ Efficiency = 4 ÷ 1 = **4 days**

⇒ Time taken by **B** to do **17-times** work = 17 × 4 = **68 days**

**∴ The correct answer is 68 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Efficiency and Work Relation

**Work** is directly proportional to **Efficiency** and **Time**. Formula: Work = Efficiency × Time.

Time and Work Reciprocal Rule

If a person completes a work in **n days**, then the work done in 1 day is **1/n** part of the total work.

Multiple Work Units

If the **amount of work** increases by **k-times**, the time required at the same efficiency also increases by **k-times**.</p

questions.question: Which of the following factors does NOT affect the rate of evaporation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Colour of the liquid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Evaporation is a process where liquid changes into vapor without boiling, and it primarily depends on the properties of the liquid and the surrounding environment.
 
• **Humidity** of the surrounding air affects the rate of evaporation. Lower humidity levels increase the rate of evaporation.
 
• **Temperature** of the liquid is a crucial factor. Higher temperatures increase the kinetic energy of molecules, speeding up evaporation.
 
• **Surface area** of the liquid plays a significant role. A larger surface area allows more molecules to escape, increasing the rate of evaporation.
 
• The **colour of the liquid** does not inherently affect the rate of evaporation. Evaporation is more dependent on physical properties like temperature and surface area.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evaporation Process:**

 
 
• Evaporation is an endothermic process where liquid molecules absorb energy to transition into the gas phase.
 
• This process occurs at the surface of the liquid and can happen at temperatures below boiling point.
 
 
 
• **Factors Affecting Evaporation:**
 
 
• Wind Speed: Higher wind speeds remove the saturated layer of air above the liquid, enhancing evaporation.
 
• Atmospheric Pressure: Lower pressure reduces the energy needed for molecules to escape into the air, increasing evaporation.
 
 
 
• **Applications of Evaporation:**
 
 
• Used in cooling mechanisms such as sweat evaporation to regulate body temperature.
 
• Important in industries for concentrating solutions and drying materials.
 
 
 
• **Evaporation vs. Boiling:**
 
 
• Evaporation occurs at the surface and at any temperature, while boiling occurs throughout the liquid at a specific boiling point.
 
• Evaporation is a slower process compared to the rapid vaporization seen in boiling.

questions.question: The electric power consumed by a resistor of resistance R, carrying current I, is _______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**I²R**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The electric power consumed by a resistor is given by the formula **P = I²R**, where P is power, I is current, and R is resistance.
 
• This formula derives from Ohm's Law, which states that V = IR (voltage = current × resistance).
 
• Using the relationship P = VI (power = voltage × current) and substituting V with IR, we get P = I²R.
 
• This equation indicates that the power dissipated in a resistor increases with the square of the current.
 
• The unit of power is the watt (W), where 1 watt equals 1 joule per second.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• A resistor is a passive electrical component that provides resistance to the flow of electric current.
 
• Resistors are used to control the current in an electric circuit.

• **Power**
 
 
• Power in an electrical circuit is the rate at which energy is consumed or converted.

questions.question: If AB = k + 3, BC = 2k and AC = 5k - 5, then for what value of ‘k’ does B lie on AC?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

If point **B** lies on the line segment **AC**, then the sum of the parts must equal the whole: **AB + BC = AC**.

⇒ (k + 3) + (2k) = 5k − 5

⇒ 3k + 3 = 5k − 5

⇒ 2k = 8

⇒ k = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Length of **AB** = k + 3

Length of **BC** = 2k

Length of **AC** = 5k − 5

**Condition:** For point **B** to lie on the line segment **AC**, the points **A, B, and C** must be **collinear** and **B** must be between **A** and **C**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e85c74aaa8404d19451dd2ec0877f0d6a2f44bd348e96f939cda680e75fb1eb1.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ AB + BC = AC

⇒ (k + 3) + 2k = 5k − 5

⇒ 3k + 3 = 5k − 5

⇒ 5k − 3k = 3 + 5

⇒ 2k = 8

⇒ k = 8 ÷ 2

⇒ k = 4

**∴ The correct answer is 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Collinearity Property

Three points are collinear if the sum of the lengths of the two shorter segments equals the length of the longest segment.

Triangle Inequality

In a triangle, the sum of any two sides must be strictly greater than the third side (AB + BC > AC). If AB + BC = AC, the triangle collapses into a straight line.

Section Formula

If B divides AC in ratio m:n, then B = (mC + nA) / (m + n). Here, the ratio AB:BC is (4+3):(2×4) = 7:8.</p

questions.question: Two trains of length 220 m and 280 m are running towards each other on parallel lines at 42 km/h and 30 km/h, respectively. In how much time will they be clear of each other from the moment they meet?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Relative Speed** (Opposite Direction) = 42 + 30 = 72 km/h.

Convert to m/s: 72 × (5/18) = 20 m/s.

**Total Distance** = Sum of lengths = 220 + 280 = 500 m.

**Time** = Total Distance ÷ Relative Speed = 500 ÷ 20 = 25 sec.

**∴ The correct answer is 25 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a4fff94c0103ce4b22cf97ffd0f446f0627d2c7d970845a4363bde56ea2cfee6.png] 

**Given:**

Length of first train (L₁) = 220 m

Length of second train (L₂) = 280 m

Speed of first train (S₁) = 42 km/h

Speed of second train (S₂) = 30 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Time = (L₁ + L₂) ÷ (S₁ + S₂)

Conversion: 1 km/h = 5/18 m/s

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Distance = 220 + 280 = 500 m

⇒ Relative Speed = (42 + 30) × (5/18) m/s

⇒ Relative Speed = 72 × (5/18) = 4 × 5 = 20 m/s

⇒ Time taken = 500 ÷ 20 = 25 seconds

**∴ The correct answer is 25 sec.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Relative Speed Concept

When two objects move in **opposite directions**, their relative speed is the **sum** of their individual speeds (u + v). When moving in the **same direction**, it is the **difference** (u − v).

Unit Conversion

To convert speed from **km/h to m/s**, multiply by **5/18**. To convert from **m/s to km/h**, multiply by **18/5**.

Train Crossing Objects

When a train crosses a **pole/man**, distance = length of train. When it crosses a **platform/bridge/another train**, distance = length of train + length of object.</p

questions.question: Which of the following compounds is used as an antacid?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Magnesium hydroxide**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Magnesium hydroxide** is commonly used as an antacid to neutralize stomach acid and relieve indigestion and heartburn.
 
• It is often referred to as "milk of magnesia" due to its milky appearance.
 
• Magnesium hydroxide works by neutralizing hydrochloric acid in the stomach, thereby increasing the pH level and reducing acidity.
 
• It is also used as a laxative to relieve constipation by drawing water into the intestines and promoting bowel movements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Antacids:**

 
 
• Antacids are substances that neutralize stomach acidity and are used to relieve heartburn, indigestion, or an upset stomach.
 
• Common active ingredients include magnesium hydroxide, aluminum hydroxide, calcium carbonate, and sodium bicarbonate.
 
• Antacids provide quick relief from symptoms but do not heal the underlying cause of acid-related conditions.
 
 
 
• **Mechanism of Action:**
 
 
• Antacids work by neutralizing the excess hydrochloric acid in the stomach, which increases the pH level and reduces acidity.
 
• This action provides relief from pain and discomfort caused by acid reflux and indigestion.
 
 
 
• **Other Uses of Magnesium Hydroxide:**
 
 
• Besides being an antacid, magnesium hydroxide is also used as a laxative to treat constipation.
 
• It works by drawing water into the intestines, which helps to soften stools and stimulate bowel movements.
 
 
 
• **Safety and Side Effects:**
 
 
• Common side effects of magnesium hydroxide include diarrhea, cramping, and an imbalance in electrolytes if used excessively.
 
• Patients with kidney disease should use magnesium hydroxide with caution due to the risk of magnesium accumulation.

questions.question: Which of the following device is governed by Flemming’s Left Hand Rule
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Electric motor**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Fleming's Left Hand Rule is used to determine the direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field, which is essential in the functioning of an electric motor.
 
• According to the rule, if you align your thumb, forefinger, and middle finger perpendicular to each other, the thumb represents the direction of force (motion), the forefinger the magnetic field, and the middle finger the current.
 
• Electric motors convert electrical energy into mechanical energy, and Fleming's Left Hand Rule helps in predicting the direction of this mechanical force.
 
• This principle is critical in various applications, including fans, washing machines, and other household appliances that use electric motors.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fleming's Right Hand Rule**

 
 
• This rule is used to determine the direction of induced current when a conductor moves in a magnetic field.
 
• It is applicable in generators, where mechanical energy is converted into electrical energy.
 
 
 
• **Electric Generators**
 
 
• Electric generators operate on the principle of electromagnetic induction to convert mechanical energy into electrical energy.
 
• They utilize Fleming's Right Hand Rule to determine the direction of induced current.
 
 
 
• **Magnetic Field**
 
 
• A magnetic field is a region around a magnetic material or a moving electric charge within which the force of magnetism acts.
 
• It is fundamental to the operation of both motors and generators.
 
 
 
• **Electromagnetic Induction**
 
 
• It is the production of an electromotive force across a conductor when it is exposed to a varying magnetic field.
 
• This principle is used in transformers, induction coils, and various other electrical devices.

questions.question: An imaginary straight line passing through the pole and the centre of curvature of a spherical mirror is called as ______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**principal axis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The principal axis is an imaginary line passing through the **pole** and the **centre of curvature** of a spherical mirror.
 
• It is used as the reference line for measuring the angles of incident and reflected rays in optics.
 
• The point where the principal axis meets the mirror surface is known as the **pole (P)** of the mirror.
 
• The principal axis helps in determining the focal length and radius of curvature of the mirror.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Centre of Curvature**

 
 
• The centre of curvature is the center of the sphere from which the spherical mirror is a part.
 
• It is denoted by the letter **C**.
 
 
 
• **Focal Point**
 
 
• The focal point, also known as the focus, is the point where parallel rays of light either converge or appear to diverge after reflecting from the mirror.
 
• It is denoted by the letter **F**.
 
 
 
• **Focal Length**
 
 
• The focal length is the distance between the pole and the focal point of the mirror.
 
• It is denoted by the letter **f**.
 
 
 
• **Radius of Curvature**
 
 
• The radius of curvature is the distance between the pole and the centre of curvature.
 
• It is denoted by the letter **R** and is equal to twice the focal length (R = 2f).

questions.question: Which organelle is the powerhouse of the cell?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mitochondria**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mitochondria are known as the powerhouse of the cell because they generate most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), used as a source of chemical energy.
 
• They are double-membrane-bound organelles found in the cytoplasm of almost all eukaryotic cells, including plants and animals.
 
• Mitochondria have their own DNA, which is inherited maternally and is used to produce some of the proteins and enzymes required for their function.
 
• They play a crucial role in cellular respiration, a process that converts biochemical energy from nutrients into ATP.
 
• Mitochondria are also involved in other processes like signaling, cellular differentiation, cell death, and the control of the cell cycle and cell growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Structure of Mitochondria:**

 
 
• Mitochondria have two membranes: an outer membrane and a highly folded inner membrane.
 
• The inner membrane folds are called cristae, which increase the surface area for ATP production.
 
 
 
• **Functions Beyond Energy Production:**
 
 
• Mitochondria help regulate the metabolic activity of the cell.
 
• They are involved in the synthesis of certain steroids and the urea cycle.
 
 
 
• **Role in Apoptosis:**
 
 
• They play a key role in programmed cell death (apoptosis), which is essential for the removal of damaged or unnecessary cells.
 
 
 
• **Genetic Diseases:**
 
 
• Mutations in mitochondrial DNA can lead to a variety of genetic disorders, often affecting the muscles and nervous system.
 
 
 
• **Evolutionary Origin:**
 
 
• The endosymbiotic theory suggests that mitochondria originated from a symbiotic relationship between a primitive eukaryotic cell and a prokaryote.

questions.question: What is the name of the connective tissue that connects two bones to each other?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ligament**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ligaments** are a type of connective tissue that connect bones to other bones in joints.
 
• They are composed of dense, fibrous connective tissue that provides stability and support to joints.
 
• Ligaments are crucial for maintaining the structure of the skeletal system and enabling proper movement.
 
• They contain collagen fibers, which provide tensile strength and elasticity to withstand various types of stresses.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tendons**

 
 
• Tendons are connective tissues that connect muscles to bones.
 
• They are composed mainly of collagen fibers and are designed to withstand tension.
 
• Tendons play a vital role in transmitting the force generated by muscles to bones, facilitating movement.
 
 
 
• **Cartilage**
 
 
• Cartilage is a flexible connective tissue found in various parts of the body, including joints, ear, and nose.
 
• It provides cushioning and reduces friction between bones in joints.
 
• There are three types of cartilage: hyaline, elastic, and fibrocartilage, each serving different functions.
 
 
 
• **Adipose Tissue**
 
 
• Adipose tissue, or body fat, is a type of connective tissue that stores energy in the form of fat.
 
• It also provides insulation and cushioning to protect organs and tissues.
 
• Adipose tissue is found beneath the skin, around internal organs, and in bone marrow.
 
 
 
• **Fibrous Connective Tissue**
 
 
• Fibrous connective tissue is characterized by a dense arrangement of collagen fibers.
 
• It includes ligaments, tendons, and the dermis layer of the skin.
 
• This type of tissue provides strength, support, and flexibility to various body structures.

questions.question: Which of the following elements is monoatomic?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Helium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Helium** is a noble gas and exists as a monoatomic gas under standard conditions.
 
• It is the second lightest and second most abundant element in the observable universe, after hydrogen.
 
• Helium atoms consist of a single nucleus with two protons and two neutrons, surrounded by two electrons.
 
• Being monoatomic, helium does not form chemical bonds with other atoms and is chemically inert.
 
• Helium's low boiling and melting points make it valuable for cryogenics and as a coolant in superconducting magnets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Noble Gases**

 
 
• Noble gases are a group of chemical elements with similar properties; in the periodic table, they are located in Group 18.
 
• They are all odorless, colorless, monatomic gases with very low chemical reactivity.
 
• The noble gases include helium, neon, argon, krypton, xenon, and radon.
 
• Due to their inertness, noble gases are used in applications where reactions with other substances are undesirable.
 
 
 
• **Helium's Applications**
 
 
• Helium is used in cryogenics, particularly in cooling superconducting magnets in MRI scanners and other devices.
 
• It is also used as a protective gas in arc welding and in the production of silicon wafers for electronics.
 
• Helium is utilized in gas chromatography as a carrier gas due to its inert properties.
 
• It is used in breathing mixtures for deep-sea diving and in balloons and airships due to its lightness and non-flammability.
 
 
 
• **Helium's Discovery and Extraction**
 
 
• Helium was first discovered in 1868 by French astronomer Pierre Janssen and English astronomer Norman Lockyer independently, through spectroscopic analysis of the Sun.
 
• Helium is extracted from natural gas deposits, where it is found in concentrations of up to 7% by volume.
 
• Most of the world's helium supply comes from natural gas fields in the United States, particularly in Texas, Oklahoma, and Kansas.

Marked Price and Discount

The **Marked Price** is the price printed on the label. **Discount** is always calculated on the Marked Price, while **Profit/Loss** is calculated on the Cost Price.

• This law states that every point mass attracts every other point mass by a force acting along the line intersecting both points.
 
• The force is proportional to the product of the two masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance between them.
 
• The formula is F = G (m₁m₂) / r², where F is the gravitational force, m₁ and m₂ are the masses, r is the distance between the centers of the two masses, and G is the gravitational constant.
 
 
 
• **Significance of G**
 
 
• It allows us to measure the gravitational force between any two bodies with known masses and distance.

• **Measurement of G**

• Modern measurements continue to refine the value using more precise methods and equipment.
 
 
 
• **Role in General Relativity**
 
 
• In Einstein's theory of general relativity, G helps describe the curvature of spacetime due to mass and energy.
 
• It plays a critical role in understanding gravitational waves, black holes, and the expansion of the universe.
